alternatives.explanation: Definitions: the invoice header bills the missing line and only the invoice-line table is incomplete, so this is a recording artefact and not lost revenue.
alternatives.test: Check every invoice line against the order lines (orphans, null line_id). Compare invoice header amount with the sum of its lines, overall and on the 3,815 orders that had some lines invoiced. Check whether billed price and qty match the order line.
alternatives.result: Ruled out. All 2,558,500 invoice lines map to an order line, none has a null line_id, and no line_id is billed twice (q357). Header and line sums never differ by more than $0.03 (q359, q361). On the 3,815 partly invoiced orders, no header differs from its lines by more than $1, and none contains the missing value (q360). Invoices bill at exactly the order-line price and shipped qty: 0 price or qty differences across 2,558,500 lines (q400). So line price is the right measure of what was not billed.

alternatives.explanation: Paid outside the invoice (cash at the counter), or the customer paid the full amount anyway, which would explain why counter is high.
alternatives.test: Look at payment methods by channel. Look for payments with no invoice. Look for overpayment on affected orders against what was invoiced.
alternatives.result: No sign of it in this ledger. Counter orders are paid by ACH and check through AR like every other channel; there is no cash method (q365). There are 0 payments without an invoice. On the 4,950 affected orders, 0 were overpaid and 0 were paid an amount equal to invoiced plus missing; 4,899 were paid exactly what was invoiced and 51 were underpaid (q367). Not testable: a counter POS or cash drawer that never reaches finance. That record is not in the warehouse.

alternatives.explanation: Timing or cut-off: lines shipped near the end of the records may simply not be invoiced yet.
alternatives.test: Measure the lag from ship to invoice for invoiced lines, by channel. Compare the rate for lines shipped in the last 20 days with earlier lines.
alternatives.result: Ruled out. Every invoiced line is billed on its ship day: lag 0 at the median, the 99th percentile and the maximum in every channel (q369). The rate for days 2501-2520 is the same as before (counter 0.953% of 2,938 vs 1.1264% of 219,454; email 0.1647% vs 0.1547%) (q371). So a line with no invoice by its ship day was never invoiced. Excluding ship_day > 2520 (the cut-off) is right.

alternatives.explanation: Confounding by customer mix: counter customers (cash or small residential trade) differ from email/phone customers, and the customer, not the channel, drives the gap.
alternatives.test: Within-customer comparison for customers who use both counter and email/phone. Rates by customer trade within channel.
alternatives.result: Survives. Among 5,520 customers who use both, counter lines go uninvoiced at 1.1244% (2,500 of 222,347) vs 0.1531% (2,478 of 1,618,133) on their email/phone lines, 7.34x (q394, q412). By trade, counter is 1.1074-1.1855% and non-counter 0.1476-0.1633% (q391).

alternatives.explanation: Mix by fulfilment within channel: counter has more of some fulfilment type that leaks.
alternatives.result: Ruled out. Counter is 1.1222-1.1597% for stock, special and transfer alike. Email is 0.1382-0.156% and phone 0.0981-0.1516%. EDI and web are 0 in every fulfilment type (q395).

alternatives.explanation: Person-level clustering hidden by channel mix: the finding's keyer range (0.2078-0.3594%) mixes each keyer's counter and non-counter share, so it could hide or create differences between keyers.
alternatives.test: Channel-adjusted dispersion across the 48 keyers: chi-square of each keyer's count against the pooled rate, separately for counter and for email/phone.
alternatives.result: No keyer stands out. Counter: keyer rates 0.762-1.6361% around a pooled 1.1241%, chi-square 36.51 on 47 df, 0 keyers beyond the 99% band. Non-counter: 0.1047-0.234% around 0.1529%, chi-square 46.91 on 47 df, 0 beyond the band (q387). That is the spread chance alone would produce. All counter, email and phone orders carry a keyer (48 each); EDI and web carry none (q382).

alternatives.explanation: Two mechanisms (a dropped line vs a whole missed order), as the finding says. Or one mechanism that only looks like two.
alternatives.test: Compare the counter line rate on single-line and multi-line orders. Count whole-order misses by order size and orders missing 2+ lines.
alternatives.result: The two-mechanism reading does not survive. 1,131 of the 1,135 whole-order misses (99.65%) are single-line orders; only 4 multi-line orders lost every line, and only 35 orders lost 2 or more lines (q385, q412). On counter, single-line orders lose 1.1272% and multi-line orders 1.1232% of lines (q381); email is 0.1546% vs 0.1549%. Interpretation: individual lines drop out at random at a channel-specific rate. A 'whole missed order' is just a one-line order that lost its line.

alternatives.explanation: Duplicate or zero-value lines (keyed twice, free goods) that were never meant to be billed.
alternatives.test: Compare price, qty and value of uninvoiced vs invoiced lines. Count lines that share an sku with another line on the same order.
alternatives.result: Ruled out. Uninvoiced lines look like ordinary lines: 0 zero-price lines, mean value $569.82 in both groups, median $246.75 vs $251.62, mean markdown 0.0109 vs 0.0116 (q375). A same-sku sibling line occurs at 1.24% of uninvoiced counter lines vs 1.35% of invoiced counter lines (q376).

alternatives.explanation: Seasonality: the leak is a winter peak.
alternatives.test: Rate by calendar month of ship day, counter vs other.
alternatives.result: The rate is flat (counter 0.975-1.212%, other 0.077-0.116% by month). The count peaks in winter (758 lines in January vs 193 in September) because counter volume peaks then (31,613 vs 8,685 counter lines) (q392). That is a volume effect, not a change in behaviour.

alternatives.explanation: Did the goods actually leave? Special-order lines have no WMS trace.
alternatives.test: Check WMS sale coverage for all shipped lines by fulfilment, not only the uninvoiced ones.
alternatives.result: Stock and transfer lines have a WMS sale 100% of the time (2,313,827 and 122,474). Special lines almost never do: 46 of 127,184 (q409). So the 234 uninvoiced special lines ($341,631.34, 12.03% of the value, q412) rest only on ERP qty_shipped. Their physical shipment is not independently confirmed.

alternatives.explanation: The money: is $285k a year recoverable?
alternatives.test: Age the uninvoiced value and check whether the customer still orders (ordered in the last 252 operating days).
alternatives.result: $285,468.20 a year is the right size of the annual leak at billed price (q325, consistent with q400). Most of the $2,840,528.65 is old: $1,740,801.83 shipped 2016-2021 and $531,175.17 in 2022-2023 (q406). Lines from 2025 total $271,314.82 and from 2024 $297,236.84 ($285,621.84 of it with customers still active), $556,936.66 together (q406, q412). Margin at static cost is about $71,523.61 a year (q325). That is the true profit effect, not the revenue figure.

alternatives.explanation: Credit memos on never-billed goods: are the $4,618.18 really credits for those lines, or other credits on the same order-day?
alternatives.test: Match each of the 16 returns to credit memos on its order and day, and compare with return qty x line price.
alternatives.result: Holds. 16 returns, 16 memos, no other returns on those order-days. Each memo equals the returned value: $4,618.18 credited vs $4,618.19 at line price (q399).

what_changed: 1) The 'two mechanisms' interpretation is withdrawn. Whole-order misses are nearly all single-line orders (1,131 of 1,135), and the counter line rate is the same on single- and multi-line orders (1.1272% vs 1.1232%). This is one mechanism: individual lines drop at a channel-specific rate. 2) The keyer evidence is replaced. The finding's range mixed in channel; the channel-adjusted spread across the 48 keyers is what chance produces (chi-square 36.51 and 46.91 on 47 df, 0 outliers). 3) The channel effect is strengthened: it holds within the same customers (1.1244% vs 0.1531%, 5,520 customers), within every trade and fulfilment type, in every month, and the line looks like any other line. 4) Ruled out with this ledger: the header hiding the line, invoicing lag, duplicate or zero-price lines, and payment collected through AR anyway. Not ruled out: off-ledger counter cash/POS. 5) The money is restated. $285,468.20 a year is revenue at billed price, but most of the $2.84M is 2016-2023 and probably not collectable. The near-term billable pool is 2025 $271,314.82 plus 2024 $297,236.84. 6) The 234 special lines ($341,631.34) have no WMS trace for any special line, so their shipment rests on ERP alone.
revised_conclusion: Leaving out lines with ship_day after the last record day (the cut-off), 4,985 shipped order lines worth $2,840,528.65 at the price invoices bill at were never invoiced, 2016-2025. That is about $285,468.20 a year (2016-2024 average), or about $71,523.61 a year of margin at static cost. Invoices are always raised on the ship day, so these lines were not late; they were never billed. The leak is a channel effect. Counter lines drop at 1.1241% (2,500 of 222,392) against 0.1548% email and 0.1477% phone, and 0 of 716,011 EDI/web lines. The gap holds for the same customers ordering both ways (1.1244% vs 0.1531%), across trades, fulfilment types, months and years. Lines drop one at a time at that rate. Interpretation: the 'whole missed orders' are one-line orders that lost their only line, and no keyer, branch or customer stands out beyond chance. Interpretation: whatever step turns a manually keyed order into invoice lines loses lines at random, much more often for counter orders. The data cannot tell whether counter goods were paid off-ledger. No cash payment method exists in finance, and affected orders were paid exactly what was invoiced, which argues against it, but a counter POS is not in the warehouse. Actions: compare a sample of counter orders against POS/cash records; run a daily shipped-not-invoiced exception report (the zero lag makes it exact); consider billing 2025 ($271,314.82) and 2024 ($297,236.84) lines with active customers; treat the older $2.27M as mostly unrecoverable.
not_evidence_of: Wrongdoing or carelessness by any keyer, branch or customer: the channel-adjusted spread across keyers is what chance produces. Not evidence that $2.84M can be collected: most of it is over two years old. Not evidence of lost profit equal to revenue: margin is about a quarter of the value. Not evidence the 234 special-order lines physically shipped: there is no WMS record. Not evidence of why lines drop: there are no invoice-run logs or edit history. Not evidence that counter customers went unpaid-for outside this ledger. The 2025 order-year count of 1,437 overstates the leak because of the cut-off.
